Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : BM4219 : Rehabilitation Engineering { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1: Fundamentals of Rehabilitation Engineering: Rehabilitation Engineering: Impairments, disabilities and handicaps and Engineering concepts in sensory and motor rehabilitation.
Module 2: Sensory Rehabilitation: Rehabilitation of vision, hearing, and speech.
Module 3: Motor Rehabilitation: Spinal rehabilitation:
Module 4: Standards and Practices in Rehabilitation: Rehabilitation engineering: principles and practices and International classification of functionality, disability health (ICF)

Course Objective

Identify and categorize different types of impairments, disabilities, and the corresponding engineering solutions.
2 .

Design and critique rehabilitation technologies aimed at enhancing sensory and motor functions.
3 .

Apply the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) to tailor rehabilitation strategies for individual needs.

Course Outcome

1 .

1. To comprehend the concepts of impairments, disabilities, and rehabilitation.
2. To apply engineering principles to design and implement rehabilitation solutions.
3. To understand the technologies and methodologies used in sensory and motor rehabilitation.
4. To evaluate the effectiveness of rehabilitation engineering in improving functionality.

8925.t: CE6245: Application of AI in Structural Optimization
8925.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CE6245 : Application of AI in Structural Optimization { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module I: Optimization problem formulation [6 hours]
Optimal Problem Formulation, Engineering Optimization Problems, Classification of Optimization Algorithms, Graphical optimization, linear programming, Simplex method.
Module II: Constraints and unconstrained optimization problems [4 hours]
Constraints and unconstrained optimization methods Single and Multi variable optimization methods:
Module III: Traditional optimization algorithms [4 hours]
Direct search method, Gradient based methods, Newton’s method, Levenberg-Marquardt’s method.
Module IV: Structural Optimization with Evolutionary algorithms [10 hours]
Introduction to Evolutionary algorithms: Need for evolutionary algorithms, Type of evolutionary methods, Genetic algorithm (GA): Real-coded GA, Multi-objective GA, Particle Swarm optimization & Teaching Learning Based Optimization techniques for truss optimization.
Module V: Introduction to ANN & Deep Learning algorithms and applications [12 hours]
ANN based approaches for structural optimization problems- Introduction- basic concept of ANN- Architectures and learning methods of NN & structural applications, Introduction to Deep Learning, Convolution Neural Network Application of AI in Structural Design and Manufacturing Data Fitting and Regression Shape, geometry and material optimization for 2D and 3D truss and frame structures AI application in Structural Health Monitoring.

Course Objective

1 .

To understand the optimal problem formulation for a given structure and learn to solve by tradition optimization methods.
2 .

To understand the working principle and application of Evolutionary algorithms for structural design application.
3 .

To apply ANN for structural design and optimization problem.
4 .

To Apply AI and Deep learning techniques for structural optimization and structural health monitoring problems.

Course Outcome

1 .

After the completion of this course, students will be able to:
CO1: Understand the basic concept of Optimal Problem Formulation
CO2: The students will be able to understand the single and multi-variable optimization methods.
CO3: The students will acquire knowledge regarding Direct search and Gradient-based optimization methods.
CO4: The students will be able to understand the concept of dealing with structural optimization problems with Evolutionary optimization algorithms.
CO5: The students will be able to apply ANN and Deep learning techniques for structural design and optimization problems.

Essential Reading

1 .

Arora,J.S., Introduction to Optimum Design, 2nd Edition,, McGraw-Hill Book Company, 2000

2 .

K. Deb, Optimization for Engineering Design: Algorithms & Examples, Prentice Hall India

Supplementary Reading

1 .

K. Deb, Multi-Objective Optimization using Evolutionary Algorithms, John Wiley & Sons

2 .

Rao,S.S., Engineering Optimization, Theory and Applications, 3rd Edition, New Age International publication, New Delhi

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CR3403 : Refractory Laboratory { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

1. Determination of packing density of one component system of various particle sizes.
2. Determination of packing density of two component system using various particle sizes having different weight ratios.
3. Determination of packing density of three component system using various particle sizes having different weight ratios.
4. Recipe calculation and recipe making for refractory mix using most packed composition.
5. Preparation of refractory brick / shape by dry pressing, drying and firing.
6. Characterization of the fired refractory brick / shape by determination of bulk density, apparent porosity and crushing strength.
7. Determination of shrinkage and PLCR of refractory brick.
8. Processing and casting of castable composition using planetary mixer and vibrator. Curing, drying and firing of the same.
9. Effect of casting parameter on the properties of castable.
10. Study of densification and strength development in the castable with temperature.

Course Objective

1 .

To provide hands-on knowledge of shaped and unshaped refractory manufacturing and characterisation techniques

2 .

To gain knowledge on the utilisation of theoretical concepts in practical refractory making
3 .

To impart and develop basic knowledge and understanding of processing and characterisation steps for refractory making.
4 .

To carry out various refractory testing and have knowledge of them

Course Outcome

1 .

Apply the knowledge gained in the theoretical course to develop and manufacture shaped and unshaped refractories in laboratory scale and their characterization

2 .

To be well versed with refractory manufacturing equipment and techniques practised in industries.

3 .

Gain hands-on experience to evaluate the properties of refractories in the laboratory, as per the standard practice used in industrial-scale operations.

4 .

Ability to design and manufacture refractories with different compositions.

5 .

Understand and implement various steps involved in refractory manufacturing methods.
6 .

Ability in report writing, presentation in a timely manner.

Essential Reading

1 .

R. Sarkar, Refractory Technology: Fundamentals and Application, CRC Press , Year 2023

Supplementary Reading

1 .

J. H. Chester, , Refractories- Production and Properties, , The Iron and Steel Institute, London ,

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CS2074 : Computer Organization Laboratory { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

1. Realization of basic logic gates using any hardware description language such as Verilog, VHDL.
2. Design a 4-to-1 multiplexer (MUX) using Verilog (VHDL ) and verify its output on various input combinations.
3. Design a 2-to-4 decoder using Verilog (VHDL).
4. Draw the truth table of the overflow/underflow detector while adding two fixed point numbers represented in 2’s complement.
5. Design the logic circuit in Verilog (VHDL), Design an SR latch.
6. State the truth table of the full subtractor. Design it in Verilog.
7. Design an 8x1 multiplexer using two 4x1 MUX, and Design 4 bit full adder circuit using four 1-bit full adders.
8. Generate G_i and P_i and S_i while adding two x_i, y_i and a carry C_i: Implement a 4-bit carry look-ahead adder.
9. Implement an 8-bit adder cascading two 4-bit carry look-ahead adders.
10. Using the case statement, design an 8-function ALU that takes 4-bit inputs a, b and 3-bit input signal select, and gives 5-bit output.
It implements the following function.
Select Signal Function
3’b000 out=a
3’b001 out=a+b
3’b010 out=a-b
3’b011 out=a/b
3’b100 out=a%b
3’b101 out=a<<1
3’b110 out= a>>1
3’b111 out=(a>b)
case ({s1,s0})
2’b00: out=xx
2’b01:out=xy
2’b10:out=xz
2’b11:out=zz
default:out=yy
endcase
Design a control unit for the GCD processor.

Course Objective

1 .

To get exposure with hardware description Language.
2 .

To implement adder circuits using basic gates.
3 .

To understand the converter circuits using basic gates.
4 .

To understand the various circuits for ALU, datapath and control units.

Course Outcome

1 .

Student should able to design and implement new digital circuit, embedded system, etc.

Essential Reading

1 .

SAMIR PALNITKAR, Verilog HDL: A Guide to Digital Design and Synthesis, Prentice Hall

2 .

Nazeih M.Botros, HDL Programming VHDL and Verilog, Dreamtech Press

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : EC6206 : VLSI Signal Processing { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Typical Signal Processing Algorithms, Overview of VLSI Architectures, Representations of DSP Algorithms. Iteration Bound, Pipelining, Parallel Processing, Definitions and Properties, General Methodology, Unfolding Algorithm, Critical Path, Unfolding, and Retiming, Folding Transformation, Register Minimization. 1 .

Learn architectures of signal processing algorithms for VLSI implementation

Course Outcome

1 .

CO1: To understand IC design flow for signal processing applications
CO2: To develop the knowledge of signal processing algorithms like Convolution, Correlation, FFT, FIR filters and the like.
CO3: To learn design of systolic architectures for above mentioned algorithms
CO4: To learn the register length precision analysis linking to performance of the algorithms.
CO5: Solve practical and state of the art signal processing algorithms using VLSI architectures to serve industries.

Essential Reading

1 .

K. K. Parhi, VLSI Digital Signal Processing Systems, Design and Implementation, John Wiley , 1999

Supplementary Reading

1 .

S.Y.Kung, VLSI Array Processors, Prentice-Hall , 1988

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : HS2350 : Game Theory in Economics { 2-0-0 / 2}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Unit – 1
Foundations: Calculus and Optimization Probability and Expectation, Utility and Expected Utility Introduction to Game Theory
Unit – 2
Strategic form Games and Dominant Strategies, Dominance Solvability, Nash Equilibrium, Applications: Cournot Duopoly, Voting and Elections, The Commons Problem Mixed Strategies and Zero-sum Games
Unit – 3
Extensive Form Games and Backward Inductions: Subgame Perfect Equilibrium, Finitely and Infinitely Repeated Games Applications – R&D, Stock Market, OPEC, and Trade Agreements
Unit – 4
Asymmetric Information Games: Moral Hazzard and Incentives Theory, Signalling Games and Lemon Problem
Basics of Dynamic Games and Cooperative Games

Course Objective

1 .

To assimilate the interconnections between Game Theory and Economics.
2 .

To understand and assess the fundamental procedures of rules of the game, forms of the game.
3 .

To analyze the applications of game theory principles in Economics and Business.
4 .

To comprehend and evaluate the different types of game theory: pure and mixed, cooperative and non-cooperative, static and dynamic.

Course Outcome

1 .

On successful completion of the course, students will be able to:
1. Identify and understand the rationale of game theory as a mathematical model
2. Apply the techniques of game theory in Economics, Business, and Finance
3. Assess the importance of different game theoretical applications in understanding fundamentals of Micro and Macroeconomics laws and theories.

Dutta Prajit K., and Vergote, W. (2022), Strategies and Games: Theory and Practice, MIT Press

Watson, J. (2013), Strategies: An Introduction to Game Theory, W. W. Norton

Romp G. (1997),, Game Theory: Introduction and Applications, Oxford University Press

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : FP3511 : Dairy Process Engineering { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Milk reception and principals of milk processing: milk storage, bulk cooling, stirring and mixing, pasteur-ization, sterilization, centrifugation, homogenization, evaporation and condensation. Spray drying of milk, principle and equipment: spray dryer, cyclone separator. Manufacturing of milk products and principles of processing of cheese, ice-cream, butter, special milk products, casein, whey, curd, butter milk etc. Equipment for indigenous milk products manufacturing. Milk ultra-filtration and reverse os-mosis. Filling Operations: Principles and working of different types of bottle filters and capping ma-chine, pouch filling machine, pre-pack and aseptic filling. Filling and Packaging machines for milk and milk products, aseptic packaging. Bulk milk handling system, care and maintenance. Hygienic design concepts, sanitary pipes and fittings, CIP system. Preventive maintenance program for Dairy Plant. Maintenance organization, development of optimum organization planned overhaul and PERT plan-ning, Utilities and sanitation in processing plant. Manufacturing of milk products and principles of processing of fluid dairy products, fat rich dairy products such as cream, butter, butter-oil, frozen dairy products such as ice-cream, fermented dairy products such as cheese and yoghurt, evaporated dairy products, dried dairy products, dairy by-products, indigenous dairy products.

Course Objective

1 .

To understand the principles of Dairy processing and milk products processing.

Course Outcome

1 .

Student will be familiarize with the processing of milk and milk products in the dairy industry.

Essential Reading

1 .

Gösta Bylund, Dairy processing handbook, Tetra Pak Processing Systems AB

2 .

A W Farrall, Engineering for dairy and food products, John Wiley and Sons

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Sukumar De, Outlines of dairy technology, Oxford University Press

2 .

Tufail Ahmed, Dairy Plant System and Layout, Kitab Mahal, Allahabad

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : MA5148 : Wavelet Analysis { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module I (8 hours)
Review of Fourier series, Fourier theory on L1 (R) and L2 (R), basic properties of windowed Fourier transform.
Module II (4 hours)
Orthonormal basis generated by a single function, Balian-Low theorem, Gabor transform.
Module III (18 hours)
Dyadic wavelets and examples, Multiresolution Analysis (MRA), scaling function and low-pass filters, construction of orthonormal wavelets from MRA, Properties of MRA wavelets, Properties/characterizations of scaling functions and low-pass filters, Spline wavelets, Daubechies wavelets, Some applications of wavelets.

Course Objective

1 .

To identify the limitations of classical Fourier analysis.
2 .

To introduce the construction/applications of wavelets with some specific examples.

Course Outcome

1 .

CO1: Students will learn about results related to convergence, term-by-term integration and differentiation of Fourier series along with some applications.
CO2. They will learn about Fourier transform on L1(R) and its extension to L2(R) along with their properties.
CO3. Students will get acquainted with the properties and characterizations of wavelets in L2(R) and they will learn about the powerful technique of MRA for the construction of wavelets.
CO4. They will see the construction of different types of wavelets such as Daubechies and Spline wavelets.
CO5. Also they will get familiar with some applications of wavelets in signal/image processing.

Essential Reading

1 .

E. Hernandeze and G. Weiss, A first course on wavelets, CRC Press

2 .

D. F. Walnut, An introduction to wavelet analysis, Birkhäuser

Supplementary Reading

1 .

G. Bachman, L. Narici, and E. Beckensterin, Fourier and Wavelet Analysis, Springer-Verlag

2 .

C.K . Chui, An Introduction to Wavelets, Academic Press

Journal and Conferences

1 .
